rounds.text: Exim Routes Ltd demonstrates exceptional historical growth, evidenced by compounded sales growth of 125% over 5 years and 72% over the trailing twelve months [E8, E10]. Profitability expansion has been equally striking, with 5-year compounded profit growth reaching 190% alongside a robust 3-year median return on equity of 33% [E11, E15]. Operating margins have also structurally improved, rising to 7% in Mar 2026 from 2% three years prior [E17]. Furthermore, the valuation offers an attractive entry point, as the stock trades at a moderate P/E of 20.1 against a DCF-derived intrinsic value of Rs 216 per share, providing a 49.6% margin of safety from the current price of Rs 109 [E1, E2, E31, E32]. A reverse DCF indicates that the current price merely prices in an 8.5% earnings growth rate, well below the 18.0% base-case assumption [E33]. Management provides clear, aggressive growth catalysts for FY27, targeting revenue between Rs 300 crores at the upper end and aiming to scale container movement to 10,000 units [E51, E52]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative to Rs -19 Cr in Mar 2026 due to working capital pressures, and institutional money flow shows a negative reading [E21, E30, E39].

Conceded: [E6]. Despite impressive reported sales and profit growth, Exim Routes Ltd suffers from a severe cash generation crisis, highlighted by negative operating cash flow of Rs -19 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -31 Cr in Mar 2026 [E21, E22]. This disconnect results in a dismal cash conversion ratio of -1.90x against reported profit [E20], meaning paper earnings are entirely failing to materialize as actual cash. Furthermore, working capital pressures are intensifying as working capital days stretched from 45.9 days to 64.4 days [E39]. Institutional confidence is actively eroding, evidenced by a massive domestic institutional stake drop of 6.05 percentage points and negative money flow [E29, E30]. Finally, borrowings have tripled to Rs 16 Cr [E25], operating margins remain inconsistent [E18, E19], and the stock pays a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4] while trading precariously at just 10% of its 52-week range [E5].

Conceded: [E20], [E21], [E22], and [E39]. While operating cash flow is negative for March 2026 and working capital days have stretched [E20, E21, E22, E39], these figures ignore the robust fundamental profitability and exceptional multi-year growth trajectory that underpins the business [E8, E11]. The reported borrowings of Rs 16 Cr are entirely offset by bank balances of more than Rs 17 Cr, demonstrating sound liquidity rather than financial distress [E25, E55]. Although domestic institutions reduced their stake, foreign institutions increased their holding, and promoters actually raised their stake to 52.64%, signaling insider and foreign confidence [E27, E28, E29]. The inconsistent annual and quarterly operating margins noted by the bear are contextualized by a multi-year structural expansion that drove operating margins up from 2% to 7% [E17, E18, E19]. Finally, the steep drop in the 52-week range [E5] combined with a conservative P/E of 20.1x [E1] and a massive valuation margin of safety [E32] shows that the market is excessively penalizing near-term working capital friction while ignoring management's ambitious FY27 guidance of up to Rs 300 crores in revenue [E51].
